Title: Diagnosis of test `testAddNonComparable`

Details: The test `testAddNonComparable` expects a `ClassCastException` to be thrown when adding a non-comparable object (a plain `Object` instance) to the frequency distribution `f`. However, this expectation is not met.

Looking at the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method, we see that it tries to add the given value `v` to a frequency table `freqTable` (likely a `TreeMap`) which requires keys to be comparable. The code handles a `ClassCastException` thrown by the `TreeMap` when `v` is not comparable, and in that catch block, it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` with a descriptive message: "Value not comparable to existing values."

Because of this, the method `addValue` will never throw `ClassCastException` itself; it will instead catch that exception and rethrow an `IllegalArgumentException`. Hence, the test failure occurs because the test expects a `ClassCastException` but an `IllegalArgumentException` is actually thrown by `addValue`.

This mismatch in expected exception types is why the test fails. The test should expect `IllegalArgumentException` to be thrown rather than `ClassCastException`.

Next, I will check if any documentation comments around `addValue` indicate the expected exception to confirm.

Title: Diagnosis of test `testAddNonComparable`

Details: The failing test `testAddNonComparable` expects a `ClassCastException` when adding a non-comparable object to the frequency distribution. However, the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method wraps any `ClassCastException` from the underlying `TreeMap` in an `IllegalArgumentException` and rethrows it. This means the method does not propagate `ClassCastException` directly, instead it throws an `IllegalArgumentException` when the value is not comparable to existing entries.

The JavaDoc for `addValue(Object)` states it throws `IllegalArgumentException` for non-comparable values and also mentions `ClassCastException`, but the actual implemented behavior is to throw `IllegalArgumentException` instead.

Hence, the root cause of the test failure is that the test expects a `ClassCastException`, but the method under test properly throws an `IllegalArgumentException`. The test needs to be updated to expect `IllegalArgumentException` for non-comparable values passed to `addValue`.

Suggested fix location:
org.apache.commons.math.stat.FrequencyTest.testAddNonComparable()

Possible alternative: If backward compatibility is a concern and the method should throw `ClassCastException`, then fix the `Frequency.addValue(Object)` method to not catch and wrap the exception. But generally, updating the test is the better approach.

---

org.apache.commons.math.stat.FrequencyTest.testAddNonComparable()
